message:
fix(update): a shell launch is not an owned launch, and the holder was asked rather than guessed

The snapshot comparison is gone. Taking a process list either side of a
shell launch and calling the single new entry "ours" is not evidence: a
user starting the same program in that window produces exactly the same
difference, and the handle opened on the strength of it does not
establish our identity, it pins a stranger's -- which a rollback would
then terminate.

The user-context launch now returns a handle. It duplicates the shell's
token and calls CreateProcessWithTokenW, which needs SeImpersonate; the
updater runs elevated and has it, which is the reason this belongs to the
updater rather than to the product. When that route fails the shell still
starts the client, but ownership is declared unknown -- nothing unknown
is terminated, and a rollback does not begin while one exists, because a
rollback moves files that process may be holding.

Refusing costs something real: the machine keeps a build it wanted to
undo. It is still the better side of the trade, and it is now a scenario
rather than an argument, with a counter-control so it cannot pass by
rollbacks simply never working.

For the backup nobody could delete, I stopped guessing. Three
explanations were proposed and each was tested and disproved -- a running
image, a lingering image section, an open process handle. Restart Manager
answers the question directly and read-only, so a surviving backup is now
reported with the name of whatever holds it. In the shape where this was
first seen, reproduced here as its own scenario, nothing survives any
more; I cannot say which of the two changes removed it and have not
claimed one.

The rename that frees a taken backup name is bounded at fifty and says so
when it runs out -- "could not move aside" alone sends someone to look at
the wrong file. And it is not a general escape: a file held open with no
sharing can be neither deleted nor renamed, so the swap stops there with
nothing half-done. All three cases are now stated rather than left to be
discovered.
